label: paragraph_title
text: ACKNOWLEDGMENT.

label: text
text: Mr. G. P. Lammert and family desire to thank their friends for the many expressions of sympathy in their bereavement and also those who attended the funeral ceremony and sent floral tributes.

label: text
text: Following a vitriolic speech by Mr. Sum Fo, Mayor of Canton, the Acting British Consul-General, at the instance of the Government of Hong Kong, has endeavoured to pin down the Canton Government in regard to its connection with the strike and the boycott. The Canton Government was asked whether it is or is not the policy of the present Canton Government to support "the Canton strikers," whether it is or is not the policy of the present Canton Government to inflict such injury as it can upon Hong Kong, and whether it is or is not the policy of the present Canton Government to "develop the anti-British boycott throughout China."

label: paragraph_title
text: MERE EVASION

label: text
text: Mr. Eugene Chen's answer to these questions is, as was only to be expected, in the negative! He endeavours to make out that Mr. Sun Fo was expressing only the views of Mr. Sun Fo, although he —Mr. Eugene Chen — never took the trouble to dissociate the Canton Government from the speech in question, which was reported as long ago as August 27. That speech opened with the phrase: "Opinions of our Party and Government regarding the Sino-British negotiations." That speech stated: "Our National Government is one which represents the people in their interests—they have still more to exert themselves to support the strike until final victory is achieved." Again, said Mr. Sun Fo, Mayor of Canton and a member of the Central Executive Council of the Government of Canton: "The National Government is a kind mother to the workmen and..., the strikers are brave sons of the National Government."

label: text
text: In every sentence he uttered Mr, Sun, Fo appears to have gone out of his way to associates the Nationalist Government with the strike and the boycott. In spite of the fact that a strict censorship

label: text
text: prevails over the vernacular newspapers in Canton the Man Kwok Yut Po was permitted to publish the speech of Mr. Sun Fo in full, apparently without the alteration of a single comma. It was made, as we have previously indicated, with the express intention of expressing the "opinions of our party and Government" and with the object of countering the condemnation of the Governor of Hong Kong concerning the Canton Government's connivance with "pirates and banditters." And from August 27 until September 16 Mr. Eugene Chen did not trouble—"even with a view to avoiding misunderstandings in present circumstances"—to let it be known that Mr. Sun Fo was speaking only for Mr. Sun Fo and not for the Canton Government which is "the kind mother of the workmen" and the father of the "brave" strikers!

label: text
text: Further argument with Mr. Eugene Chen would be futile. A realm of proofs would be met with a foolscap of negatives. But he has yet to be taught that the British Government will no longer tolerate either outrages by the pickets or the continuance and spread of the anti-British boycott.

text: [To the Editor of the "China Mail"] Sir,—Though we may all acknowledge certain of these Chinese militarists to be "notorious," yet I do not think that it is at all just for us to have an idea that their wives must necessarily be the same.

text:
"Ionides" evidently has none of

Therefore, no matter what are our feelings against the men, it is only an act of courtesy on our part that we should term the ladies "Mesdames," for, as far as we know, they take no part in the management of their husbands' affairs.

text: HELLO, KOWLOON!

label: paragraph_title
text: CHOKED DRAINS.

label: paragraph_title
text: CONTRACTOR WHO RECEIVED CURSES:

label: text
text: SUMMONS NOW WITHDRAWN.

label: text
text:
Appearing before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning for the defendant in a building prosecution, Mr. L. R. Andrews referred to his case as the one in which a contractor was cursed at by his client's people. The owner of the building was summoned for failing to carry out some work which resulted in the choking of drains in a side lane. On the ground that the contractor was well paid to carry out the work properly, it was suggested at the previous hearing that he should be held responsible. It was also stated that the people looking after the interests of the owner who was away in Canton had properly cursed the contractor for his negligence.
Mr. Grimes, of the P.W.D., said he was now satisfied that everything was in order.
CORRESPONDENCE ON PHONE SERVICE

label: text
text:
The summons was accordingly withdrawn.
K.R.A. & THE COMPANY.

label: text
text: Some time ago a sub-committee was appointed by the Kowloon Residents' Association to investigate the cause of certain complaints which had been received regarding the telephone system in Kowloon.

label: text
text: When the sub-committee reported it was thought that they had discovered just where the trouble centred, namely, the overloading of positions on the switchboard so that the operators have more lines than they can efficiently handle.

label: text
text: Correspondence was entered into with the Hong Kong Telephone Co., with the object of confirming the sub-committee's finding "and the hope of eliciting assurances that improvements would be made at the earliest possible date.

label: text
text: Unfortunately co-operation in this direction on the part of the Telephone Co. was not forthcoming and the Committee consider that it is only fair to themselves that the correspondence should be published that the public may know the efforts they have made.

label: text
text: This decision was arrived at by the last meeting of the Committee.

label: text
text: Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Dear Sirs,—At a meeting of the general committee of the above Association, it was stated that at the central telephone exchange a minimum of 120 incoming lines were allotted to each position, whereas in some cases the number is 140 and even a few cases 160. It was also stated that the National Telephone of Great Britain will not allow a position to carry more than 100 incoming lines.

label: text
text: It was further stated that in both the exchanges, Hong Kong & Kowloon subscribers above uncertain number have not yet been allotted any position on the main switchboard, but are carried on temporary switchboards which practically constitute subsidiary exchanges.

label: text
text: I am directed by the Committee to enquire whether these statements are correct.

label: text
text: In view of the heavy load which each position carries and consequent increased strain on the operators' entailing risk of inefficient service, and in view of the apparent want of foresight during recent years resulting in lack of provision for new subscribers, the Committee would be glad to be enlightened as to the developments which are now contemplated so that they may be assured that these defects will be remedied.

label: paragraph_title
text: Other Faets Wanted.

label: text
text: The company's reply reads:— May 27.

label: text
text: It is not possible to attempt a comparison only in terms of the number of lines allotted per operator as it is essential to know the calling rate and other traffic data before a true comparison can be made. For example, an exchange with a calling rate of 1 can bear twice the number of lines per operator as an exchange with a calling rate of 2 and still give an equal service with no greater strain on the operators.

label: text
text: With reference to the extension switchboards at Central and Kowloon, in the former case work is in progress which, when completed, will allow the lines to be transferred to the main switchboard. The extension switchboard at Kowloon is only a temporary measure and it is the intention to take this out of service at the earliest possible moment.

label: text
text: Referring to the last paragraph of your letter we would advise you that it was not due to lack of foresight that development was retarded but due (a) to the impossibility of our predecessors obtaining telephone materials during the war years and for some considerable time after the cessation of hostilities (b) failure of negotiations by the China & Japan Telephone & Electric Co., Ltd. for a revision of rates and renewal of licence to secure long tenure and make the heavy capital expenditure necessary for development economically justifiable.

label: text
text: Cross-Harbour Addition:

label: text
text: As regards future development by this company this will be carried out in accordance with the Telephone Ordnance 1925, and the preliminary work necessary in this respect is even now engaging our attention. A step in this direction has been made by the laying down on the 4th instant, of a new submarine cable across the harbour to provide additional junction facilities between Hong Kong and Kowloon.

label: text
text: The necessary work of connecting up this cable has now been completed and the improvement in the service in this respect must be evident to the members of your association.

label: text
text: Agum the K.R.A. wrote:—

label: text
text: July 12.

label: text
text: Telephone Co.: Ltd.

label: text
text: Dedrs Sirs,—I am to thank you for your letter of May 27, in reply to ours of May 6, but at the same time explain that it does not altogether meet the questions raised.

label: text
text: It might be as well to explain at the outset how these questions arose. The Committee of the Kowloon Residents' Association received complaints about the working of the telephone system and, while some attributed the faults to the inefficiency of the operators, others defended the operators and blamed the conditions under which they worked. It was stated that the number of lines allotted to a single operator was abnormally high, even as high as 140 or 160 in several instances. Thus the Committee was led to inquire whether these figures were correct. Your answer omits to name the maximum loads for a single position and, therefore, misses the point of the Committee's inquiry.

label: text
text: We note, however, that you admit that the average per operator is 124, and justify that high figure by the pleur that the calling rate must be taken into account. But, as the subscribers to your telephone are not limited in their calls, can you deny that the calling rate in this Colony, and particularly in Kowloon is a high one, and consequently, the position is made worse by the introduction of this factor into the calculation?

label: text
text: Comparison was made with the National Telephone Co. of Great Britain in the belief that the system used by that now defunct company was similar to the anti-quated system is use in Hong Kong.

label: text
text: With regard to the second paragraph of our letter, the Committee are glad to have a satisfactory reply.

label: paragraph_title
text: The New Rates.

label: text
text: With regard to the final part of our inquiry, let me explain that it arose in this way. It was stated in defence of the Telephone Co. that the space occupied by them at present is so cramped that there is no room for proper development. It was, therefore, decided to ask for some assurance that the company was likely soon to extend and reorganise its undertaking. We are now told that a step has been taken in this direction by the laying down of a new cable across the harbour. As my Committee understand that this new cable replaces one that was laid by your predecessors, are they to conclude that, although a year has elapsed since the new company was formed and the higher subscription rates were introduced, this is the only forward movement worth mentioning that has been made so far?

label: paragraph_title
text: Company's Assurance.

label: text
text: I duly received your letter of July 12, 1926 and regret that owing to extreme pressure of business I have not hitherto been able further to consider the matter with a view to forwarding you a reply.

label: text
text: I have now, as a matter of fact, referred your letter of May 6, 1926, my reply thereto of May 27 and your further letter of July 12, to my board of directors, and they feel that no good purpose could be served by a continuation of correspondence on the lines of such letters. The board quite appreciate and sympathise with the object which prompted you to communicate with the company, but beg to point out that the company's desire for improvement in the telephone service in Kowloon is at least equally as strong as that of the Residents' Association.

label: text
text: You must therefore kindly excuse me from replying point by point to your letter of July 12, and permit me to assure you that all that can reasonably and practically be done to effect both immediate and ultimate improvements and extensions is being done.

label: text
text: Moon-enke fenst., or the mid-autumn festival, was appropriately celebrated by the Chinese yesterday, inclement weather notwithstanding.

label: text
text: A European has asked if the festival is religious. As explained in Monday's "China Mall," the origin is mithyical but not religious, but the worshipping of the full moon may be regarded as a form of religion.

label: text
text:
Firecrackers were heard. 11 day. Fancypaper lanterns were lit. in the majority of houses and West Point was on fete for the occasion. Nearly every tenhouse sold out its stock of mooncakes.
Through carelessness in worshipping, occupants of a house in the western district had to flee during a midnight service as a fire had broken out.

label: text
text: The day is also one of the four settling days of the Chinese year. On a restricted scale, and with events as generally anticipated some days before, there was no unusual development. It was felt that money is plentiful but not circulating normally.

label: text
text: We are now told that a further postponement until November is necessary to enable the Investigating Committee to complete their work.

label: text
text: Meanwhile shareholders are left absolutely in the dark, and I cannot help feeling that this great delay is detrimental to the business of the company and the interests of shareholders.

label: text
text: Let us get the past squared up as quickly as possible, write off the necessary loss, and concentrate our energies on building up the future of the company.

label: text
text: The foregoing remarks are of necessity made without knowledge of faults, and are founded on various rumours which are common property, and I may be doing the members of the Investigating Committee an injustice in offering these criticisms on their voluntary work, but I should like to ask whether this work takes the form of trying to attach blame to the Consulting Committee, or whether it is an honest attempt to assist this committee in bringing things to a satisfactory conclusion.

label: text
text: Can you therefore, Sir, give to this meeting an estimated cost of what the total expenses of this investigation will amount to, and also any information in advance of the full report of the Investigating Committee, which will help to restore public confidence in the company and allay shareholders' fears?

label: text
text:
"Not Be Too Hard!"
Mr. Shewan's reply was:—
I quite agree with your remarks as to getting the past cleared up as soon as possible, but we must not be too hard on the investigation committee. They have put a great deal of work into examination of intricate and involved accounts with which they were of course not familiar and naturally it has taken a great deal of time.

label: text
text: Mr. da Roza has explained to me how he arrives at the date November 12 and from what he tells me I feel pretty sure that this will be the last postponement and the report will be in shareholders' hands before that date.

label: text
text: As to information in advance of the full report I can say nothing except that I understand that the committee of investigation have had the cargo in godowns carefully checked by an independent surveyor and that they are quite satisfied with the management of the godowns.

label: text
text:
As to the accounts I have nothing to say at present and am sorry I cannot give you the information.
It is not easy to calculate the total expenses of the investigation but on a rough estimate we think it will come to about $40,000 or over, at any rate under $50,000.
I think I have answered all your questions.

label: text
text: On being put to the meeting, the resolution of postponement (as stated) was carried without dissent.
